# self-evaluate

The last thing every build agent does before it hands off. No worker output is trusted until it has graded its own work against the criteria it committed to — and that grade is what drives the model-routing escalation decision. This skill is the bridge between "I produced something" and "@critic should look at it".

## Description

`self-evaluate` is the mandatory final gate in every worker agent's run. It takes the agent's declared **Done Criteria** (the checklist the agent committed to at the start, sourced from the PBI acceptance criteria via `ado-context` and the architect's task shape) and grades the **current working diff** against each one.

For every criterion it emits a verdict (`PASS` / `FAIL`), the **evidence** that justifies the verdict (file:line, test output, contract field, grep hit), and a **confidence** in `[0.0, 1.0]`. It then rolls up an overall result and a `should_retry` signal.

Two downstream consumers depend on its output:
- **`model-routing-policy`** reads per-criterion confidence. A self-eval confidence `< 0.7` is one of the two escalation triggers (the other being two `@critic` FAILs) that bumps the agent ONE rung up the Haiku→Sonnet→Opus ladder.
- **`budget-policy` / `@supervisor`** read `should_retry` to decide whether a retry is affordable before the stage proceeds.

This skill **NEVER** caches. It MUST run fresh against the diff that exists at hand-off time, because the diff is the very thing it is grading.

## Inputs

- `done_criteria` (required) — the agent's committed checklist. Each item: `{ id, statement, source }` where `source` traces back to a PBI acceptance criterion, an architect sub-task, or a guardrail (e.g. `path-policy`, `dedup-policy`, `contract`).
- `diff` (required) — the current uncommitted working diff for the change (`git diff` + new untracked files). This is the artifact under evaluation; it is read fresh every invocation.
- `agent_id` (required) — the worker being evaluated (e.g. `@codegen`, `@mfe`, `@bff-shaper`); used to apply role-appropriate evidence expectations and to label the run-log entry.
- `current_tier` (required) — the agent's current model tier, so the escalation hint can name the next rung.
- `test_results` (optional) — output from `@tester` / `@integration-tester` / `@contract-tester` if the criterion is test-backed.
- `budget_remaining` (optional) — token/tool-call headroom from `budget-check`; gates whether `should_retry` can be `true`.

## Outputs

A structured self-evaluation object:

- `criteria[]` — one entry per Done Criterion:
  - `id` — the criterion id.
  - `verdict` — `PASS` | `FAIL`.
  - `evidence` — concrete proof: `path:line`, a test name + result, a contract field, a grep match. NEVER a bare assertion.
  - `confidence` — float in `[0.0, 1.0]` for THIS criterion.
- `overall` — `PASS` only if every criterion is `PASS`; otherwise `FAIL`.
- `min_confidence` — the lowest per-criterion confidence (the value `model-routing-policy` checks against `0.7`).
- `should_retry` — `true` iff `overall == FAIL` AND `budget_remaining` allows a retry; `false` otherwise.
- `escalation_hint` — if `min_confidence < 0.7` and budget allows, names the next tier up from `current_tier` (never down). Advisory only; the actual escalation decision belongs to `model-routing-policy` / `@supervisor`.

## Tools Needed

- `Read` — read the diffed/changed files to gather evidence.
- `Bash` — produce the fresh diff (`git diff`, list untracked files) and read test output; read-only with respect to source.
- `Grep` — confirm presence/absence of required symbols, imports, route guards, contract fields.

This skill does NOT write, edit, or run tests itself — it only reads and grades. Test authoring/running belongs to the tester agents.

## Constraints

- **cacheable: false (MUST run fresh against current diff).** The diff is the evaluated artifact; a cached verdict would grade stale code. Per `cache-policy`, self-eval output is on the never-cache list alongside writes, tests, and LLM completions. Do not wrap this skill in `cache-lookup`.
- **Evidence-bound.** Every verdict MUST cite concrete evidence. A `PASS` with no `path:line` / test / grep proof is itself a defect — downgrade to `FAIL`.
- **No self-promotion.** This skill may only flag a need to escalate via `escalation_hint`; it can never change its own tier or skip `@critic`. `model-routing-policy` forbids auto-downgrade and limits escalation to one rung.
- **Honest scoring.** Confidence reflects strength of evidence, not optimism. When unsure, score low — a low score is the intended signal that pulls in a stronger model, not something to avoid.
- **Path/safety aware.** Evaluate that the diff respects `path-policy` (right MFE / `eq-one-shared` / `eq-one-design-system` / BFF `src/domains/<name>/`) and `safety-rails` (no secrets, no PII in logs); a violation is an automatic criterion `FAIL`.
- **fail_modes:**
  - `missing-done-criteria` — agent handed off without a declared checklist → return `overall: FAIL`, `should_retry: true` (criteria must be declared before grading).
  - `empty-diff` — nothing changed but criteria expected output → `overall: FAIL` with evidence "no diff".
  - `unverifiable-criterion` — a criterion cannot be checked from the diff/tests (e.g. needs a running env) → mark `FAIL` with `confidence` low and evidence "unverifiable from diff"; let `@critic` / `@supervisor` adjudicate rather than guessing `PASS`.
  - `budget-exhausted` — `overall: FAIL` but no headroom → `should_retry: false`; hand the failing report to `@supervisor` for the go/no-go call.

## When to invoke

- ALWAYS, as the **final step** of every build/worker agent's run, immediately before hand-off to `@reviewer` / `@critic`. Pairs with `dna-precheck`, which every build agent runs FIRST; `self-evaluate` is the matching bookend that runs LAST.
- Applies to `@codegen`, `@mfe`, `@shared-curator`, `@design-system`, `@state`, `@contract`, `@domain-folder`, `@bff-shaper`, `@downstream-connector`, `@contract-publisher`, and any other agent that mutates the working tree.
- After a retry, invoke again on the new diff — never reuse the prior verdict.

## How it works

1. Receive `done_criteria`, `agent_id`, `current_tier`, and (optionally) `test_results` / `budget_remaining`. If `done_criteria` is empty, return the `missing-done-criteria` fail mode immediately.
2. Generate the **fresh** diff via `Bash` (`git diff` plus a listing of new untracked files). Never read a cached diff.
3. For each criterion, use `Read` / `Grep` (and any provided `test_results`) to find concrete evidence for or against it. Map test-backed criteria to their test name + result.
4. Assign `verdict` and `confidence` per criterion, attaching the evidence string. A verdict with no evidence is recorded as `FAIL`.
5. Apply guardrail checks against the diff (`path-policy`, `safety-rails`); any violation forces that criterion to `FAIL`.
6. Roll up: `overall = PASS` iff all `PASS`; compute `min_confidence`; set `should_retry = (overall == FAIL) AND budget allows`.
7. If `min_confidence < 0.7` and budget allows, set `escalation_hint` to the next rung above `current_tier` (advisory; `model-routing-policy` decides).
8. Return the structured object. The agent attaches it to its hand-off; `@supervisor` logs it to the run log for human review.

## Example

`@bff-shaper` finishes shaping the `payments` response. Its Done Criteria, current tier `sonnet`:

```
DC-1  Response shape matches PBI AC-2 (camelCase, no nulls)        source: ado-context
DC-2  No business logic added — BFF paint/polish only              source: architect
DC-3  Lives under src/domains/payments/                            source: path-policy
DC-4  Contract regenerated for @contract-publisher to pick up      source: contract
```

Fresh self-eval against the diff:

```jsonc
{
  "criteria": [
    { "id": "DC-1", "verdict": "PASS", "evidence": "src/domains/payments/Shapers/PaymentShaper.cs:41 maps to camelCase DTO", "confidence": 0.92 },
    { "id": "DC-2", "verdict": "PASS", "evidence": "diff adds mapping only; no downstream calls or branching added", "confidence": 0.88 },
    { "id": "DC-3", "verdict": "PASS", "evidence": "all changed files under src/domains/payments/", "confidence": 0.99 },
    { "id": "DC-4", "verdict": "FAIL", "evidence": "no change to payments.openapi.yaml — contract not regenerated", "confidence": 0.64 }
  ],
  "overall": "FAIL",
  "min_confidence": 0.64,
  "should_retry": true,            // budget_remaining allows it
  "escalation_hint": null          // min_confidence 0.64 < 0.7 BUT failure is mechanical (missing regen), not judgment — retry on same tier first
}
```

`@supervisor` reads `should_retry: true`, the agent regenerates the contract on the same `sonnet` tier, and `self-evaluate` runs fresh again on the new diff before hand-off to `@critic`.

## Anti-patterns

- **Caching the result.** Defeats the entire purpose; the verdict must track the live diff. (`cacheable: false`.)
- **Evidence-free PASS.** "Looks correct" is not evidence. Cite `path:line`, a test, or a grep hit, or mark `FAIL`.
- **Confidence inflation.** Reporting `0.95` to dodge escalation hides risk and starves `model-routing-policy` of the signal it needs. Score honestly.
- **Grading without declared criteria.** If the agent never committed Done Criteria, there is nothing to grade — fail fast, don't invent criteria.
- **Substituting for `@critic`.** Self-eval is the worker's own check; it never replaces the adversarial `@critic` gate or the `@supervisor` go/no-go.
- **Retrying with no budget.** `should_retry` must respect `budget-policy`; never loop a failing agent past the ceiling.
